text: Walk to the Park
Help your hero walk safely to the park with a grown-up.
We are walking to the park with Dad.
We come to the end of the sidewalk.
What do we do at the edge of the street?
Stop at the edge and hold Dad’s hand.
Stop at the edge.
Hold a grown-up’s hand near cars.
Run across fast.
Running into the street is not safe.
Cars can come fast.
Always stop first.
Now we cross the street.
Wait for the walking person sign.
Look left, look right, look left again.
Oh no!
Your ball rolls into the street.
What should you do?
Let the ball go.
Ask Dad to get it.
A ball is not worth getting hurt.
A grown-up can get it safely.
Run into the street to get it.
Never run into the street, even for a ball.
Ask a grown-up.
A lady is walking a big dog.
You want to pet it.
What should you do first?
Ask, Can I pet your dog?
Always ask the owner first.
Some dogs do not like to be touched.
Hug the dog right away.
A dog you do not know might be scared.
Ask the owner first.
We made it to the park safely!
Great job, hero!
Lost at the Store
You can’t see your grown-up.
Find help the hero way.
You are at the store.
You look up.
You can’t see Mom.
Stop.
Stay where I am.
Take a deep breath.
Stop and stay put.
It is easier for Mom to find you.
Run around the store looking.
Running around makes you harder to find.
Go out to the parking lot.
Never leave the store.
Cars are outside.
Stay inside.
Mom is still not here.
You need a helper.
Who is a safe helper at the store?
A store worker with a name tag.
Workers with name tags, or the person at the cash register, are safe helpers.
Someone in the parking lot.
Look for a worker with a name tag.
You find a worker with a name tag.
What do you say?
I am lost.
My name is Alex.
I can’t find my mom.
Say you are lost and say your name.
That helps them help you.
Say nothing and walk away.
Use your words.
Say, I am lost, and say your name.
The worker says, Stay with me.
I will call your mom on the speaker.
What do you do?
Stay with the worker and wait.
Stay with the safe helper until your grown-up comes.
Go look for Mom by myself.
Stay with the helper.
Mom is on her way.
Mom is here!
You stayed calm and found a safe helper.
Hero job!
Smoke Alarm!
The smoke alarm is beeping.
Get out and stay out.
Beep!
The smoke alarm is loud.
It is OK to cover your ears.
Get out of the house.
When the alarm beeps, get out fast.
Cover your ears if it is too loud.
Hide under my bed.
Never hide.
Firefighters need to find you.
There is smoke in the hall.
How do you move?
Get low and crawl under the smoke.
Smoke goes up.
The air is cleaner down low.
Crawl out.
Stand up tall and walk slowly.
Smoke is up high.
Get low and crawl.
You come to a door.
You touch it with the back of your hand.
It feels hot.
Do not open it.
Use another way out.
A hot door means fire is behind it.
Go another way.
Open the door fast.
A hot door means fire.
Keep it closed and go another way.
You are outside!
Your family has a meeting spot by the big tree.
Where do you go?
Go to the meeting spot and stay there.
Go to your meeting spot so your family knows you are safe.
Go back inside for my toy.
Never go back inside.
Toys can be replaced.
You can’t.
You got out and stayed out.
Firefighters are proud of you!
Pool Day
Have fun at the pool and follow the water rules.
You see the pool.
It looks so fun!
What do you do before you get in?
Wait for a grown-up to say yes and watch me.
Only swim when a grown-up is watching you.
Jump in right away.
Wait for a grown-up.
Never swim alone.
The ground by the pool is wet.
Walk slowly.
Wet ground is slippery.
Walk, don’t run.
Run fast.
You could slip and fall.
A friend is splashing in the deep water.
They look scared.
They need help.
Yell for a grown-up.
Throw a float.
Get a grown-up and throw something that floats.
Do not jump in.
Jump in to grab them.
Jumping in can hurt you both.
Yell for a grown-up and throw a float.
You hear thunder.
Boom!
Get out of the water right away.
Thunder means lightning.
Get out of the water and go inside.
Keep swimming.
Lightning is dangerous in water.
Get out now.
What a safe pool day!
You followed every water rule.

Sharp knife
Knives are sharp.
Don’t touch.
Tell a grown-up.
Hot pan on the stove
The stove is hot.
Stay back.
Only grown-ups cook.
Cleaning spray

Don’t touch it.

Teddy bear

Small batteries

Open window

TV

Campfire
Stay back from fire.
Let grown-ups take care of it.
Ball

Kite
Flying a kite is fun.
Tree

Stay on the phone.

Camino al parque

Para en la orilla.

Quieres acariciarlo.
¿Qué haces primero?

Hero Route, Spot the Danger and Practice 911 Call follow approaches studied for teaching safety skills to autistic learners , the hero models each step first (video modeling), then the learner rehearses with instant, gentle feedback (behavioral skills training), and wrong answers always lead to the safe choice (errorless learning).

For Parents & Educators
Background on Safety Superheroes, how to use it alongside a learner, and resources to go further.
About Safety Superheroes
Safety Superheroes is a free, browser-based collection of independent-living safety lessons for autistic learners and anyone who benefits from clear, predictable practice.
There is no sign-in and nothing is installed , every lesson combines a short illustrated story with a decision point, a flashcard review, and a video with built-in comprehension checkpoints.
How to use it with a learner
Sit with the learner for the first pass through a topic so you can pause on any step and talk it through in your own words.
The stories are intentionally short and low-stimulation , no timers, no flashing effects, and every wrong answer gets a calm explanation instead of a fail state.
Flashcards are a good stand-alone warm-up or review once a story has been completed once.
Resources & further reading
A starting set of outside organizations, guides, and video-based programs that pair well with Safety Superheroes.
None of these are run by Safety Superheroes , they’re independent resources we found reputable and worth sharing.

Who built this app, and why.
About the creator
Safety Superheroes was created by Evan Park, a student at Stanford University.
Why I built this
This project was created for my twin brother, Sean, who is autistic.

Growing up, Sean did not pick up everyday safety habits the way many children do simply by observing the people and world around him , knowing what to do around someone he doesn’t know, how to cross a street safely, or what to do in an emergency required direct, structured teaching and a great deal of repeated practice.
Safety Superheroes was built to meet that need:

a free tool that breaks core safety skills into short stories, flashcards, and guided practice that can be revisited as many times as necessary, at a pace that fits the learner, in English or Spanish.
Questions or feedback?
If you’re using Safety Superheroes with a learner and have feedback, questions, or a suggestion, I’d like to hear from you.

Privacy Policy
Safety Superheroes is built to need as little information about you as possible.
Here is exactly what that means.
No accounts, no logins
You never create an account or sign in to use Safety Superheroes.
There is no username, password, email address, or profile stored anywhere for using the app.
Everything stays on your device

Your preferences (color theme, text size, language, Calm Mode, sound on/off, and saved practice paths) and your progress (which lessons you’ve completed, favorites, game best streaks) are saved only in your browser’s local storage, on your own device.
None of it is uploaded to a server, and I cannot see it.
Clearing your browser’s site data for Safety Superheroes will erase it, and using a different device or browser starts fresh.
No ads, no analytics tracking, no selling data
Safety Superheroes has no advertising, no third-party analytics or tracking scripts, and no social media pixels.
There is nothing to sell, because nothing about you is collected in the first place.
Works offline, by design
Once you’ve visited the site, a service worker saves the app’s files so it keeps working without an internet connection.
This is a standard web feature (a Progressive Web App) and does not involve sending any additional information anywhere.
A note for parents and educators

Because Safety Superheroes doesn’t collect names, birthdates, contact information, photos, audio, or any other personal information from any user , child or adult , there is nothing to request the deletion of.
If you have questions about how this app handles data, or a request related to a specific device, reach out using the contact below.
Changes to this policy

If this policy ever changes , for example, if a future feature needed to collect information it doesn’t today , this page will be updated first, and the change will be described clearly, in plain language.
Questions?
If anything here is unclear, or you have a question about privacy, reach out any time.

Sobre esta biblioteca

Biblioteca de Seguridad es una colección gratuita, basada en el navegador, de lecciones de seguridad para la vida independiente, pensada para personas autistas y para cualquiera que se beneficie de una práctica clara y predecible.
No requiere iniciar sesión ni instalar nada , cada lección combina una historia ilustrada breve con un punto de decisión, un repaso con tarjetas y un video con pausas de comprensión integradas.
Cómo usarla con un estudiante
Acompañe al estudiante la primera vez que recorra un tema, para poder pausar en cualquier paso y explicarlo con sus propias palabras.

Las historias son intencionalmente breves y de baja estimulación , sin temporizadores, sin efectos parpadeantes, y cada respuesta incorrecta recibe una explicación tranquila en lugar de un estado de fallo .
Las tarjetas funcionan bien como calentamiento independiente o repaso después de completar una historia por primera vez.
Recursos y lecturas adicionales
Un punto de partida de organizaciones externas, guías, y programas basados en video que combinan bien con Superhéroes de la Seguridad.

Acerca de Safety Superheroes
Quién creó esta aplicación, y por qué.
Sobre el creador
Safety Superheroes fue creado por Evan Park, estudiante de la Universidad de Stanford.
Por qué creé esto
Este proyecto fue creado para mi hermano gemelo, Sean, quien es autista.

Mientras crecía, Sean no adquirió los hábitos de seguridad cotidianos de la misma manera en que muchos niños lo hacen, simplemente observando a las personas y el mundo a su alrededor , saber qué hacer frente a alguien que no conoce, cómo cruzar una calle de forma segura, o qué hacer en una emergencia requería una enseñanza directa y estructurada, y mucha práctica repetida.
Safety Superheroes fue creado para responder a esa necesidad:

una herramienta gratuita que divide las habilidades de seguridad esenciales en historias cortas, tarjetas de práctica, y ejercicios guiados que se pueden repasar tantas veces como sea necesario, al ritmo que se ajuste al estudiante, en inglés o español.
¿Preguntas o comentarios?
Si usas Safety Superheroes con un estudiante y tienes comentarios, preguntas, o una sugerencia, me gustaría saber de ti.

Política de Privacidad
Safety Superheroes está diseñado para necesitar la menor cantidad de información posible sobre ti.
Esto es exactamente lo que eso significa.
Sin cuentas, sin inicios de sesión
Nunca creas una cuenta ni inicias sesión para usar Safety Superheroes.
No se guarda ningún nombre de usuario, contraseña, correo electrónico, ni perfil para usar la aplicación.
Todo se queda en tu dispositivo

Tus preferencias (tema de color, tamaño de texto, idioma, Modo Calma, sonido activado/desactivado y rutas de práctica guardadas) y tu progreso (qué lecciones has completado, favoritos, mejores rachas de los juegos) se guardan solo en el almacenamiento local de tu navegador, en tu propio dispositivo.
Nada de esto se sube a un servidor, y yo no puedo verlo.
Borrar los datos del sitio de Safety Superheroes en tu navegador lo eliminará, y usar un dispositivo o navegador diferente empieza desde cero.
Sin anuncios, sin rastreo de análisis, sin vender datos
Safety Superheroes no tiene publicidad, ni scripts de análisis o rastreo de terceros, ni píxeles de redes sociales.
No hay nada que vender, porque no se recopila nada sobre ti desde el principio.
Funciona sin conexión, por diseño
Una vez que has visitado el sitio, un service worker guarda los archivos de la aplicación para que siga funcionando sin conexión a internet.
Esta es una función web estándar (una Aplicación Web Progresiva) y no implica enviar información adicional a ningún lado.
Una nota para padres y educadores

Como Safety Superheroes no recopila nombres, fechas de nacimiento, información de contacto, fotos, audio, ni ninguna otra información personal de ningún usuario , niño o adulto , no hay nada que solicitar eliminar.
Si tienes preguntas sobre cómo esta aplicación maneja los datos, o una solicitud relacionada con un dispositivo específico, contáctame usando la información de abajo.
Cambios a esta política

Si esta política cambia alguna vez , por ejemplo, si una futura función necesitara recopilar información que hoy no recopila , esta página se actualizará primero, y el cambio se describirá con claridad, en lenguaje sencillo.
